neighbours.label: the additive step in 'may also …' / 'can also be …' when a sentence adds a further case to a parallel statement just made
fire: You may need this scan if you have chest pain. You may also need this scan if you have fainted.
Broken hips are emergencies. Deep cuts can also be emergencies.
You may get this form if you changed jobs. You may also get this form if you moved abroad.
Loose wires are hazards. Wet floors can also be hazards.
You may have this blood test if you feel tired. You may also have this blood test if you bruise easily.
Late frosts are threats to the crop. Dry winds can also be threats.
You may be given this drug if you have a fever. You may also be given this drug if you have a cough.
Unpaid bills are warning signs. Missed calls can also be warning signs.
quiet: You may need this scan if you have chest pain. Tell the nurse when it started.
Broken hips are emergencies. Call for help at once.
You may get this form if you changed jobs. Send it back within a month.
Loose wires are hazards. Report them to the manager.
You may have this blood test if you feel tired. It takes five minutes.
Late frosts are threats to the crop. Farmers cover the vines at night.
You may be given this drug if you have a fever. Take it with water.
Unpaid bills are warning signs. Keep a list of them.

notes: Card: may be, may also, can also be, 'A third category of', 'The second danger'. Probes: 'You may also have this test' 0.40 after a parallel sentence, 'can also be emergencies' 0.24, 'A second category of' 0.20; controls 0.01-0.08. Weak pole.
